items.title: Section: Opening — and the Three Difficult Practices

items.zh: 云何菩薩難行戒？當知此戒略有三種。謂諸菩薩，現在具足大財、大族自在增上，棄捨如是大財、大族自在增上，受持菩薩淨戒律儀。是名菩薩第一難行戒。又諸菩薩受淨戒已，若遭急難乃至失命，於所受戒尚無少缺，何況全犯。是名菩薩第二難行戒。又諸菩薩，如是如是遍於一切行住作意，恒住正念，常無放逸，乃至命終於所受戒無有誤失，尚不犯輕，何況犯重。是名菩薩第三難行戒。
items.en: From the Bodhisattva Stage within the Basic Section, the chapter on the discipline of the initial yoga foundation, part three. What is a bodhisattva's difficult practice with regard to discipline? One should know this precept is, in brief, of three kinds. Bodhisattvas who presently possess great wealth, an eminent family, and genuine worldly power and independence, yet give up all of that wealth, family standing, and independence in order to take up and hold the bodhisattva precepts — this is called a bodhisattva's first difficult practice. Bodhisattvas who, having received the precepts, encounter an emergency or grave danger, even to the point of losing life itself, and yet find not the slightest compromise in the precepts they hold, let alone an outright violation — this is called a bodhisattva's second difficult practice. Bodhisattvas who, in this way and that, across every moment of walking, standing, and all other activity, constantly abide in mindfulness, remaining forever free of carelessness, right up until the moment of death, finding no error at all in the precepts they hold — not violating even a minor precept, let alone a grave one — this is called a bodhisattva's third difficult practice.

items.title: Section: The Four Comprehensive-Gateway Precepts — Formal Reception, Innate Nature, Habituation, and Skilful Means

items.zh: 云何菩薩一切門戒？當知此戒略有四種。一者、正受戒，二者、本性戒，三者、串習戒，四者、方便相應戒。正受戒者，謂諸菩薩受先所受三種菩薩淨戒律儀。即律儀戒、攝善法戒、饒益有情戒。本性戒者，謂諸菩薩住種性位，本性仁賢，於相續中，身語二業恒清淨轉。串習戒者，謂諸菩薩昔餘生中，曾串修習如先所說三種淨戒。由宿因力所住持故，於現在世一切惡法不樂現行，於諸惡法深心厭離；樂修善行，於善行中深心欣慕。方便相應戒者，謂諸菩薩依四攝事，於諸有情身語善業恒相續轉。
items.en: What is a bodhisattva's comprehensive-gateway precept? One should know this precept is, in brief, of four kinds. First, the precept of formal reception; second, the precept of innate nature; third, the precept of habituation; fourth, the precept of skilful means. The precept of formal reception is when bodhisattvas properly receive the three bodhisattva precepts already described — namely, the precept of discipline, the precept of gathering wholesome dharmas, and the precept of benefiting sentient beings. The precept of innate nature is when bodhisattvas, abiding within the bodhisattva lineage prior even to formal reception, are by innate nature kind and virtuous, their bodily and verbal conduct remaining constantly pure throughout the continuity of their being. The precept of habituation is when bodhisattvas, having already practised and habituated themselves to these same three precepts across former lifetimes, find that the power of that prior cause now sustains them, such that in the present life they take no pleasure at all in unwholesome conduct, feel deep aversion towards it, and instead delight in wholesome conduct, feeling deep and genuine enthusiasm for it. The precept of skilful means is when bodhisattvas, relying on the four means of gathering beings, keep their bodily, verbal, and mental conduct constantly and continuously directed towards benefiting all beings.

items.title: Section: The Five Virtuous-Person Precepts — What Makes Someone a Genuine Spiritual Friend

items.zh: 云何菩薩善士戒？當知此戒略有五種。謂諸菩薩自具尸羅，勸他受戒，讚戒功德，見同法者深心歡喜，設有毀犯如法悔除。
items.en: What is a bodhisattva's virtuous-person precept? One should know this precept is, in brief, of five kinds: bodhisattvas themselves genuinely hold the precepts; they encourage others to receive the precepts; they praise the precepts' genuine benefits; seeing fellow practitioners who hold the same precepts, they feel deep and genuine joy; and should a lapse ever occur in their own conduct, they properly confess and correct it without delay.

items.title: Section: The Comprehensive-Kind Precepts Open — Six Ways the Precepts Themselves Are Complete

items.zh: 云何菩薩一切種戒？當知此戒以要言之，六種，七種，總十三種。言六種者，一、迴向戒，迴向大菩提故。二、廣博戒，廣攝一切所學處故。三、無罪歡喜處戒，遠離耽著欲樂、自苦二邊行故。四、恒常戒，雖盡壽命亦不棄捨所學處故。五、堅固戒，一切利養恭敬、他論、本隨煩惱不能伏故、不能奪故。六、尸羅莊嚴具相應戒，具足一切戒莊嚴故。尸羅莊嚴如聲聞地應知其相。
items.en: What is a bodhisattva's comprehensive-kind precept? One should know this precept, in brief, comes to thirteen kinds altogether — six of one sort and seven of another. The six are: first, the precept of dedication, since it is dedicated towards supreme awakening. Second, the precept of breadth, since it comprehensively includes every area of training. Third, the precept of blameless joy, since it steers clear of both indulgent attachment to sensory pleasure and self-punishing austerity. Fourth, the precept of permanence, since it is not abandoned even when this life comes to an end. Fifth, the precept of firmness, since it cannot be overcome or stolen away by any offering of support and reverence, any rival doctrine, or any root or secondary affliction. Sixth, the precept that functions as an ornament, since it fully possesses the qualities of every kind of adornment a precept can offer — a nature of adornment one should understand in the same way as described in the Śrāvaka Stage.

items.title: Section: Seven Fruits the Precepts Produce — Culminating in a Heart That Naturally Loves Beings

items.zh: 言七種者，一、止息戒，遠離一切殺生等故。二、轉作戒，攝一切善故，饒益有情故。三、防護戒，隨護止息轉作戒故。四、大士相異熟戒。五、增上心異熟戒。六、可愛趣異熟戒。七、利有情異熟戒。
items.en: The seven are: first, the precept of ceasing, since it steers entirely clear of killing and every other harmful act. Second, the precept of actively doing, since it comprehensively gathers every wholesome deed and genuinely benefits sentient beings. Third, the precept of guarding, since it protects and sustains both the precept of ceasing and the precept of actively doing. Fourth, the precept that ripens into the marks of a great being. Fifth, the precept that ripens into a settled, elevated mind. Sixth, the precept that ripens into rebirth in genuinely favourable circumstances. Seventh, the precept that ripens into a heart that benefits sentient beings as its own nature.

items.title: Section: The Fulfilling-Requests Precepts — the Golden Rule as Formal Discipline

items.zh: 云何菩薩遂求戒？當知此戒略有八種。謂諸菩薩自諦思惟：如我悕求勿彼於我現行斷命，不與而取，穢欲邪行，虛妄，離間，麁惡，綺語，手塊杖等諸非愛觸加害於我。我求是已，他若相違而現行者，我求不遂、我意不悅。如我悕求，他亦如是。勿我於彼現行斷命，廣說乃至惡觸加害。彼求是已，我若相違而現行者，彼求不遂、彼意不悅。我之所作，若有令他所求不遂、意不悅者，何現行為。菩薩如是審思惟已，命難因緣亦不於他現行八種所求不遂、不悅意事。如是八種，說名菩薩遂求戒。
items.en: What is a bodhisattva's fulfilling-requests precept? One should know this precept is, in brief, of eight kinds. Bodhisattvas honestly reflect in this way: "Just as I myself hope that no one will take my life, take what is not given to them, engage in defiled and improper sexual conduct towards me, speak falsely to me, speak divisively of me, speak harshly to me, speak idle and meaningless words at me, or strike, stone, or beat me, or inflict any other unwelcome physical harm upon me — having wished for this, if another acts against my wish, what I hoped for is not fulfilled, and my mind is unhappy. Just as I myself hope for this, so too does every other being. They too hope that I will never take their life," and so on in full detail down to inflicting unwelcome physical harm, "and having wished for this, if I act against their wish, what they hoped for is not fulfilled, and their mind is unhappy. If anything I do leaves another being's hope unfulfilled and their mind unhappy, why would I ever act this way?" Having reflected honestly in this way, bodhisattvas do not, even under threat to their own life, inflict upon others these eight kinds of unfulfilled hope and unhappiness. These eight, taken together, are called a bodhisattva's fulfilling-requests precept.

items.title: Section: The Both-Worlds-Happiness Precepts Open — Four Precepts of Discerning Judgement

items.zh: 云何菩薩此世他世樂戒？當知此戒略有九種。謂諸菩薩為諸有情，於應遮處而正遮止，於應開處而正開許，是諸有情應攝受者正攝受之，應調伏者正調伏之，菩薩於中身語二業常清淨轉，是則名為四種淨戒。
items.en: What is a bodhisattva's precept of happiness in this world and the next? One should know this precept is, in brief, of nine kinds. For the sake of beings, bodhisattvas correctly restrain what should genuinely be restrained, and correctly permit what should genuinely be permitted; among beings, they correctly draw in those who should genuinely be drawn in, and correctly correct those who genuinely require correction — bodhisattvas conducting themselves throughout with bodily and verbal action that remains constantly and genuinely pure. These are called the four kinds of pure precept.

items.title: Section: Five Precepts Pairing Discipline With Every Other Perfection — Both-Worlds-Happiness Closes

items.zh: 復有所餘施、忍、精進、靜慮、般若波羅蜜多俱行淨戒，則為五種。總說名為九種淨戒。如是菩薩所有淨戒，能令自他現法後法皆得安樂，是故說名菩薩此世他世樂戒。
items.en: There are, further, pure precepts that proceed together with the perfections of generosity, patience, diligence, meditative concentration, and wisdom — these make five more kinds. Together with the four already named, these are called, in total, the nine kinds of pure precept. In this way, all of a bodhisattva's pure precepts enable both oneself and others to attain genuine ease in this present existence and in lives to come — and it is for this reason that this is called a bodhisattva's precept of happiness in this world and the next.

blocks.text: Fascicle 42 completes the perfection of discipline with the remaining aspects of its nine-part frame, then covers the perfections of **patience** and **diligence**. These lists are compact; each aspect is a different angle on the same practice.

Bodhisattvas "who possess great wealth, an eminent family, and worldly power renounce them" to take up the precepts; keep them even "in urgent danger, up to danger to life"; and keep even the smallest rule. Master Cháng Bǎi: what is hard to give up is given up; what is hard to practise is practised.
Discipline by formal reception; by innate nature (Venerable Miào Jìng: some people are kind and good by nature, before any teaching); by habituation from past lives; and joined with skilful means.

"Keeping the precepts oneself, encouraging others to receive them, praising their benefits, rejoicing when others keep them, and correcting lapses." Master Cháng Bǎi: the spirit of the precepts is compassion: not harming beings.

Thirteen kinds. Among them, "the precept of the blameless place of joy, avoiding the extremes of sensual indulgence and self-torment"; precepts kept "even when life ends" (Master Cháng Bǎi: to the end of future time); "the precept of ceasing" from harm and "the precept of actively doing" good (keeping by refraining and keeping by acting); and finally, "a heart that naturally loves beings".
"Just as I myself hope for life and happiness, so do others; if I act contrary to that, their wish is frustrated." So bodhisattvas do not harm.

"Restraining what should be restrained, permitting what should be permitted, drawing in those who should be drawn in, correcting those who should be corrected." And discipline joined with each of the other perfections: keeping the precept against killing is also the gift of fearlessness (Master Cháng Bǎi).

quiz.q: How does Master Cháng Bǎi sum up why these are called "difficult" precepts?
options: worldly fortune hard to give up is given up; what is hard to practise is practised
quiz.why: Master Cháng Bǎi: worldly blessings that are hard to give up are given up, and what is hard to practise is practised — hence "difficult precepts."

quiz.q: What are the four comprehensive-gateway precepts?
options: formal reception, innate nature, habituation, skilful means
quiz.why: "First, the precept of formal reception; second, the precept of innate nature; third, the precept of habituation; fourth, the precept of skilful means." Master Cháng Bǎi: a gate is for going in and out — through all these gates one keeps the bodhisattva precepts.

quiz.q: The innate-nature precept: "abiding in the stage of lineage, innately kind and good." How do the two lectures explain this?
options: Miào Jìng: "innate" means without dharma conditioning — kindness and goodness by nature; Cháng Bǎi: like a bean seed which, with sun, fertilizer, and water, can sprout
quiz.why: Venerable Miào Jìng: "innate" means originally — without dharma conditioning, the person's nature is already kind and good; "rén" is kindness, "xián" is goodness. Master Cháng Bǎi: like a bean seed that, planted and given sunlight, fertilizer, and water, is able to sprout.

quiz.q: What are the five virtuous-person precepts?
options: keeping the precepts oneself, encouraging others, praising them, rejoicing at fellow practitioners, and confessing any lapse
quiz.why: "Bodhisattvas themselves genuinely hold the precepts; they encourage others to receive the precepts; they praise the precepts' benefits; seeing fellow practitioners they feel deep joy; and should a lapse occur they confess it properly." Master Cháng Bǎi: staying away from the ten unwholesome deeds is "keeping the precepts oneself."

quiz.q: Among the seven, what is "the precept of ceasing"?
options: steering clear of killing and all harmful acts
the marks of a great being
quiz.why: "First, the precept of ceasing, since it steers entirely clear of killing and every other harmful act." Master Cháng Bǎi: precepts that stop harming beings — this is "keeping by refraining."

quiz.q: What is the reasoning behind the fulfilling-requests precept?
options: just as I wish not to be harmed, so do others; harming them would frustrate their wish, so I do not
quiz.why: "Just as I hope … so do others. … If I act contrary to that, their wish is frustrated and they are displeased." Master Cháng Bǎi: the precept that satisfies both oneself and others.

quiz.q: On precepts proceeding with generosity, how does Master Cháng Bǎi explain discipline accompanying the gift of fearlessness?
options: all beings fear death; keeping the precept against killing is discipline together with giving fearlessness
quiz.why: Master Cháng Bǎi: all beings fear death; keeping the precept against killing is discipline proceeding together with the gift of fearlessness. Venerable Miào Jìng: when giving there is also discipline; when being patient there is also discipline.
